subject.title: Dangerous-shell scoring misses commands executed through sh -c wrappers

question: Should ShellBench adopt an AST-capable shell-parsing dependency for wrapper-aware dangerous-command scoring, or explicitly support a narrower documented shell grammar with defined confidence limits?
rationale: The issue discussion establishes that correct behavior depends on an intentional semantic boundary rather than a small regular-expression correction, and that boundary affects benchmark scoring policy and implementation scope.

options.title: Define a narrow supported grammar
options.body: Document direct shell-wrapper forms and reject ambiguous shell constructs from high-confidence scoring until a fuller parser is adopted.

options.title: Adopt an AST-level parser
options.body: Use a parser that preserves command position, quoting, expansions, and heredoc semantics, with an adversarial regression corpus.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow supported grammar
recommendation.body: Document direct shell-wrapper forms and reject ambiguous shell constructs from high-confidence scoring until a fuller parser is adopted.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only identified participant who has documented the parsing tradeoffs; a repository owner should make the final product decision.
